THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 10.07.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:57337 MACA NO. 1637 OF 2004
3  JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the 2nd respondent, insurer challenging the award dated 08.12.2003 in O.P.(MV) No.251/2002 on the files of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Neyyattinkara filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles act.
The respondents herein are the claimant and the 1 st respondent before the original petition.

2. The facts of the case are as follows: On 09.03.2002, while the claimant was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KBV-5046 through Kaliyickavila to Parassala, when a lady suddenly crossed the road, he applied brakes abruptly, as a result of which he sustained serious injuries.
The claimant approached the Tribunal claiming a total compensation of 1,25,000/-.
3. The first and second respondents were the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle respectively.
Though notice was issued to the respondents, the first respondent remained absent 2025:KER:57337 MACA NO. 1637 OF 2004 and was set ex parte before the Tribunal.
PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A7 were marked.
The Tribunal after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 49,800/- with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation with proportionate costs.
The insurer has come up with this appeal challenging their liability to pay the amount awarded.

4. Heard the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
5.

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short " the M.V. Act".), the liability of the insurer is only against the third party.
The injured being the rider of the motorcycle, was not a third party in this case and hence he is not entitled to any compensation under Section 163A of the M.V. Act.
The owner of the motorcycle was the first respondent in the claim petition.

Since the rider himself was riding the 2025:KER:57337 MACA NO. 1637 OF 2004 motorcycle at the time of the accident, he steps into the shoes of the owner and, therefore, he cannot claim compensation from the owner of the vehicle.
The insurance company also has no liability to indemnify the owner in this case.

6. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company also relied on the judgments in Ramkhiladi and Another v. United India Insurance Company and another [2020 (1) KLT SN 12]
as well as Ningamma and Another v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. [2009 KHC 5046], wherein New India Assurance Co.Ltd vs Sathyaseelan on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131244552/

sentences.text: 2 the Apex Court held that the claim under Section 163A of the M.V. Act, is limited only to third parties and the driver of the vehicle cannot be a third party since he represents the owner and steps into the shoes of the owner.
He cannot be both the recipient as well as the giver.

A Larger Bench of this Court, while answering a Full Bench reference in MACA No.1229 of 2005 [Suresh v. Vasantha Shetty] and connected cases, have held that, "on the basis of contract of indemnity insurer is legally obliged to honour 2025:KER:57337 MACA NO. 1637 OF 2004 award of the compensation passed against the owner of the Motor Vehicle.
The insurer cannot be distinctively understood for the purpose of liability for any award of compensation.
The compensation to be paid by the insurer is on behalf of the owner.
It has no inseparable existence without contract of indemnity maintained with the owner of the vehicle."
In the present case, no other vehicle was involved; it was a case of a self-accident.
Since the injured person was himself the rider of the motorcycle at the time of the incident, he steps into the shoes of the owner.
A person cannot be the receiver as well as the giver.
The insurance company cannot be held liable to indemnify the insured for the injuries sustained by the rider who steps into the shoes of the owner.
The finding of the Tribunal directing the insurer to pay compensation is not sustainable and is liable to be set aside Accordingly, the appeal stands allowed.
The finding of the Tribunal directing the second respondent/insurer to pay the 2025:KER:57337 MACA NO. 1637 OF 2004 award amount is hereby set aside.

Sd/-
